scope: Focused FMO hard-negative/counteraxis review over existing 702-label artifacts, current flavin_dehydrogenase_reductase rows, and relevant OOS/boundary rows.

selected_oos_or_boundary_rows_inspected.selection_reason: expert-reviewed flavodiiron NO reductase relabel; flavin-cofactor leakage negative
oxygenase name without flavin C4a-peroxy support
heme peroxidase-like oxygen chemistry outside FMO

positive_fmo_axis_not_negative_controls.axis_definition: Clean FMO requires flavin-dependent O2 activation to a C4a-(hydro)peroxyflavin or equivalent flavin peroxy oxygenating intermediate, followed by substrate oxygen insertion/oxygenation.
positive_fmo_axis_not_negative_controls.policy_note: m_csa:551 and m_csa:973 are not hard negatives; the acquisition closure treats them as clean FMO secondary/future rows while blocking primary promotion until n>=6 and hard-negative separation are satisfied.

control_groups.why_it_is_not_fmo: These rows use flavin for hydride or electron transfer between substrate, nicotinamide, quinone, disulfide, ferredoxin, or fumarate acceptor/donor partners. They do not use an activated flavin peroxy intermediate to insert oxygen into substrate.
shared_features_with_fmo: NADH or NADPH in some rows
disambiguating_evidence: Current canonical labels place all representative rows in flavin_dehydrogenase_reductase, not flavin_monooxygenase.
Packet 3 demoted the broad flavin.dehydrogenase_oxidase_hydride_transfer child because it mixed multiple flavin chemistries and was unsafe for v2 metrics.
FMO acquisition closure defines clean FMO by C4a-peroxy flavin oxygenation, not by flavin or NADPH presence alone.
control_groups.recommended_regression_gate: An FMO route is a regression for this group unless mechanism evidence explicitly shows flavin-dependent O2 activation to a C4a-(hydro)peroxyflavin and substrate oxygen insertion. Otherwise route to flavin_dehydrogenase_reductase.

control_groups.why_it_is_not_fmo: These rows may consume O2 or peroxide during flavin oxidase/peroxidase turnover, but O2 acts as an electron acceptor or peroxide partner rather than a flavin-derived oxygen atom inserted into substrate.
disambiguating_evidence: The current FMO support pool is only m_csa:131 and m_csa:132 canonically, while these rows remain current flavin_dehydrogenase_reductase rows.
The acquisition closure flags m_csa:551 and m_csa:973 as clean FMO candidates because they form C4a-hydroperoxyflavin; ordinary oxidase rows lack that oxygen-insertion evidence.
Packet 3 explicitly preserves a separate FMO acquisition question rather than absorbing oxygen/oxidase flavins into FMO.
control_groups.recommended_regression_gate: Rows with O2 as terminal acceptor, peroxide detoxification, or oxidase naming must not pass the FMO gate without explicit C4a-peroxy oxygen-transfer evidence.

control_groups.why_it_is_not_fmo: Fe-S plus flavin relay rows use Fe-S clusters for electron transfer or coupled substrate reduction chemistry. HCAR keeps FAD at the catalytic substrate-reduction locus with two 4Fe-4S clusters relaying electrons from ferredoxin; it is not flavin peroxy oxygen insertion.
disambiguating_evidence: The Fe-S population review found 9 Fe-S plus flavin rows in the old v1 flavin bucket and separated clean hydride-transfer, electron-transfer-coupled, covalent-adduct, and radical classes.
m_csa:990 is explicitly kept as v1 flavin_dehydrogenase_reductase with cofactor_complexity=fe_s_plus_flavin and mechanism_class=coupled_dehydration_and_reduction.
Packet 3 blocks the mixed hydride-transfer child until cofactor-complexity and mechanism-class axes are carried in diagnostics.
control_groups.recommended_regression_gate: For Fe-S plus flavin rows, require explicit flavin peroxy oxygenating chemistry before any FMO route. If Fe-S is an electron relay and the flavin role is substrate reduction or electron transfer, route to flavin_dehydrogenase_reductase with cofactor_complexity diagnostics.

control_groups.why_it_is_not_fmo: The catalytic locus is a non-heme Fe(II)Fe(II) carboxylate-bridged center that reduces nitric oxide. FMNH2 donates electrons to a di-iron nitrosyl complex, but flavin is not forming an oxygenating C4a-peroxy intermediate and is not the substrate oxygen-insertion locus.
disambiguating_evidence: The m_csa:497 label revision relabeled it from flavin_dehydrogenase_reductase to out_of_scope.
The decision basis names the mechanism locus as a non-heme Fe(II)Fe(II) carboxylate-bridged center.
Wave 1.1 excludes m_csa:497 from primary v1 flavin metrics and retains it only as OOS/boundary/future-acquisition signal.
control_groups.recommended_regression_gate: m_csa:497 must fail any FMO positive gate. A non-abstaining FMO call on this row is a hard regression; preferred behavior is reject as OOS until a dedicated flavodiiron NO reductase family exists.

control_groups.why_it_is_not_fmo: The mechanism is radical dehydration: FAD semiquinone radical anion abstracts a substrate C-H hydrogen, the substrate hydroxy group coordinates an Fe-S iron, and Fe-S participates in polarization/elimination. This is radical flavin/Fe-S chemistry, not flavin peroxy oxygen insertion.
disambiguating_evidence: The m_csa:750 label revision relabeled it from flavin_dehydrogenase_reductase to out_of_scope.
The decisive evidence lists FAD semiquinone C3 hydrogen abstraction, substrate hydroxy coordination to Fe-S iron, and Fe-S participation in elimination.
Wave 1.1 excludes m_csa:750 from primary v1 flavin metrics and from learned-representation canary use.
control_groups.recommended_regression_gate: m_csa:750 must fail any FMO positive gate. If FAD semiquinone plus Fe-S radical dehydration evidence is present, reject as OOS/future radical-flavin-Fe-S dehydratase rather than route to FMO or ordinary flavin reductase.

control_groups.why_it_is_not_fmo: FAD is mechanistically central, but the defining chemistry is covalent FAD-substrate adduct formation and sulfur-oxygen bond cleavage/reduction, not O2 activation to a flavin peroxy intermediate followed by oxygen insertion into substrate.
shared_features_with_fmo: possible Fe-S/flavin context in broader APS reductase-like systems
disambiguating_evidence: The Fe-S/flavin population review keeps m_csa:123 as v1 flavin with boundary metadata.
The same review assigns mechanism_class=covalent_fad_substrate_adduct and defers the current hydride-transfer v2 sublabel.
Packet 3 demotes the broad flavin hydride child partly because covalent FAD-adduct chemistry would otherwise be conflated with ordinary hydride transfer and FMO-like flavin chemistry.
control_groups.recommended_regression_gate: m_csa:123 and APS-reductase-like covalent FAD-adduct rows must not route to FMO. Route to flavin_dehydrogenase_reductase with boundary metadata or abstain in child-label settings unless a dedicated covalent-FAD-adduct stratum exists.

control_groups.why_it_is_not_fmo: These rows use heme iron or heme-derived oxidizing intermediates, not flavin C4a-peroxy chemistry. Oxygenase or monooxygenase naming is insufficient when the oxygen activation locus is heme.
shared_features_with_fmo: NADPH-linked electron supply in some systems
disambiguating_evidence: m_csa:133, m_csa:699, and m_csa:795 are current heme_peroxidase_oxidase seed rows, not flavin_monooxygenase.
m_csa:601 is current out_of_scope and was retained outside current seed fingerprints.
The FMO acquisition closure screened out m_csa:133 as P450 heme monooxygenase, not flavin monooxygenase.
control_groups.recommended_regression_gate: Heme ligation, P450/peroxidase/heme oxygenase mechanism evidence, or compound-I-like oxygen activation must route away from FMO even when the row is an oxygenase or monooxygenase.

control_groups.why_it_is_not_fmo: These controls are oxygenases or luciferase-like oxygen-consuming enzymes whose oxygen activation depends on ATP/luciferyl-adenylate, non-flavin metal centers, pterin/non-heme iron, copper, or other non-flavin chemistry rather than flavin C4a-peroxy oxygenation.
disambiguating_evidence: The acquisition closure screened out m_csa:128, m_csa:134, m_csa:135, m_csa:600, and m_csa:768 as not clean flavin C4a-peroxy FMO rows.
m_csa:129 and m_csa:130 are current out_of_scope oxygenase rows in the 702-label registry.
The required FMO discriminator is flavin-dependent peroxy oxygenation; oxygenase naming and O2 consumption alone are insufficient.
control_groups.recommended_regression_gate: Non-flavin oxygenases, dioxygenases, luciferase oxygenations, pterin/non-heme iron hydroxylases, copper monooxygenases, and soluble methane monooxygenase-like metal systems must reject as FMO unless flavin C4a-peroxy evidence is directly present.

recommended_global_regression_gates: Do not treat FAD/FMN, NAD(P)H, O2, Fe-S, or oxygenase naming as sufficient for FMO.
Require explicit flavin-dependent O2 activation to a C4a-(hydro)peroxyflavin or equivalent flavin peroxy oxygenating intermediate plus substrate oxygen insertion for FMO.
Route ordinary flavin hydride-transfer, flavin oxidase, and Fe-S relay rows to flavin_dehydrogenase_reductase, carrying cofactor_complexity and mechanism_class diagnostics where available.
Reject current OOS relabel controls m_csa:497 and m_csa:750 for FMO; do not count them in primary flavin metrics.
Keep covalent FAD-adduct chemistry out of FMO and out of the blocked hydride-transfer child metric until a dedicated stratum is acquired.
Route heme oxygenases/P450/peroxidases to heme_peroxidase_oxidase when that family is available; reject non-flavin oxygenases that have no current target family.
Preserve m_csa:551 and m_csa:973 as clean secondary/future FMO acquisition candidates, not hard-negative controls, until n>=6 and hard-negative separation are met.
non_claims: This artifact imports no labels and edits no registries.
This artifact creates no thresholds, countable metrics, model outputs, model training jobs, or production scoring changes.
Control groups are review-only regression signals and should not be used as automatic label edits.
FMO primary promotion remains blocked by the existing acquisition closure until enough clean rows and hard-negative separation evidence exist.
